reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to confirm nilotinib engaged BCR-ABL. However, nilotinib is a well-established BCR-ABL inhibitor, so target engagement is likely but unconfirmed in this trial. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers or pharmacodynamic markers reported to confirm downstream kinase signaling inhibition. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (4-month PFS rate) was not met. Overall 4-month PFS rate was low at 4.0%, with subgroup analysis showing 27% in patients without CNS metastases and 12.5% in those with CNS metastases. No p-values reported but effect sizes suggest minimal clinical benefit. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Clear subgroup difference - patients without CNS metastases had better outcomes (27% vs 12.5% 4-month PFS rate, 3.4 vs 2.4 months median PFS, 14.2 vs 4.3 months OS). This suggests the mechanism may have some activity in the non-CNS metastatic population. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm trial with small sample size (N=20) makes it difficult to assess true drug effect. No control arm for comparison. The rationale for using a BCR-ABL inhibitor in melanoma (which typically lacks BCR-ABL mutations) was weak to begin with.
